clue.text: With very different opinions, except for East Europeans

parts.note: Poles are natives of Poland, in eastern Europe
apart from, i.e. except for, gives the word apart

explanation.surface: Some East Europeans are the exception to a group who otherwise disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people at opposite ends of an argument are as far separated as the earth's two extremities, an idiom for total disagreement.

clue.text: Forwards parcel

explanation.surface: Sending a package on.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the forwards together form the scrum's pack; a parcel or bundle of goods is also a pack.

clue.text: Shelters the last remnants

explanation.surface: Somewhere safe houses whatever is left at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee is a sheltered side, so shelters in the plural; the sediment left at the bottom of a wine bottle is the final residue.

clue.text: Wonderful term for replacement

parts.note: super is an informal word for wonderful
a session is a term, as of a court or parliament

explanation.surface: Someone praises a word meaning substitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplanting one thing by another is a formal synonym for substitution.

clue.text: Dog eats nothing for tea

indicators.note: a dog that eats something takes it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a peke is a Pekingese dog
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A hungry dog wolfs down nothing at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade of black tea made from young leaves, a type of Indian or Sri Lankan brew.

clue.text: Some more trousseaux turned up

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few extra bridal outfits appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of a nose, the French borrowing means tilted upwards at the tip.

clue.text: Bird, black one, is around

indicators.note: the word is is placed around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dark bird stands nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird with a curved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Describing life from the beginnings, book is often explicit

indicators.note: the beginnings of the three following words are their first letters, picked out in turn

parts.note: graphic means vividly explicit, as of violent or sexual detail

explanation.surface: A book, read from the start, is often too explicit.
explanation.definitionFit: A biography is the written account of a person's life, so this adjective concerns such accounts.

clue.text: Spill the beans about a small honour bribery produced

indicators.note: the confession word goes about, i.e. around, the other letters

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
wee is Scottish for small
in bridge the ten is one of the honour cards, with ace, king, queen and jack

explanation.surface: An informer reveals that a minor award was obtained by bribery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'honour' is a bridge term: the five top cards of a suit, ace down to ten, are the honours.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is a bribe, so a payment or inducement given to win favour.

clue.text: Man's embracing English girl-he's a curmudgeon

indicators.note: the word for the man's holds the letter for English inside it

parts.note: a chap is a man, so chap's gives these letters
Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man hugs an English girl, though he is a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightwad or miser is the sense intended for the grumpy, mean old person.

clue.text: Rather a saintly character

explanation.surface: Someone is rather a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather can mean to a greater degree; Sir Thomas, Henry VIII's chancellor, was canonised as a saint.

clue.text: Lady not finishing speech in mitigation

indicators.note: the lady's name loses its final letter, so it is not finished

parts.note: Amelia is a woman's name
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A woman stops short in a speech pleading for leniency.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvement or lessening of something bad is a close synonym for easing.

clue.text: Former editor qualified for an award

indicators.note: qualified means modified or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A one-time newspaper editor deserved an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A British honour conferred by the monarch, limited to 24 members, for distinction in arts, science or service.

clue.text: Acclaimed a reorganization of the college

indicators.note: the letters are reorganized into a new order, which signals an anagram here

explanation.surface: A university restructuring was widely praised.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to a university or academy, as academical dress.

clue.text: Worried that it grew unassailable

indicators.note: worried in the sense of disturbed or shaken, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone frets that something kept growing.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument that cannot be faulted is figuratively sealed against leaks.

clue.text: Non-stop support in this foreign ship

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, placed inside it

parts.note: ce is French for this
an easel is a stand that supports a painting
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Continuous backing aboard a foreign vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Unending or continual, something that never pauses.

clue.text: Object about crude note written in large letters

indicators.note: the word for object goes about, i.e. around, the other letters

parts.note: an end is an aim or object
gross means coarse or crude
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A complaint about a vulgar memo printed in capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross a document is to write it out in a large formal hand, as for a legal deed.

clue.text: Young Pooter makes a bloomer

explanation.surface: A youth from a comic novel is a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Diary of a Nobody by George and Weedon Grossmith, the diarist Charles Pooter's son is called Lupin.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Pooter's son in the Grossmiths' Victorian comic diary; also a garden plant with tall spikes of flowers.

clue.text: 2 doctors come round for instance

indicators.note: the doctors come round, surrounding the other letters

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, so DRS for several
eg (exempli gratia) means for instance

explanation.surface: Two physicians visit, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' is a cross-reference: the definition is the answer to 2 Down, whose second sense is sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: The other entry's sense of sediment at the bottom of a cask matches this word for the final residue.

clue.text: A choice of men to describe the calendar

parts.note: Greg is a man's name
or introduces a choice between alternatives
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: Picking between names for a calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The calendar introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582 is the one now used in most of the world.

clue.text: Fabulous being almighty cool under stress

indicators.note: letters placed under stress are bent out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A powerful being stays calm under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its old sense means belonging to fable or legend.

clue.text: I would find Douglas here, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM

explanation.surface: Someone expects to meet a man called Douglas somewhere, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of phrase or expression peculiar to a language.

clue.text: Dress one prince up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Ras is an Ethiopian title for a prince or ruler
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single royal gets dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A draped garment worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Talking a lot, entertain lavishly

indicators.note: talking means the words are as they are spoken, a soundalike

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A chatterbox throws an extravagant party.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone with celebration and festivity.

clue.text: A hundred years in prison

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A century behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell or enclosure for confinement, as with bars.

clue.text: Become like me? It is, alas, implausible

indicators.note: something implausible is twisted from the truth, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that another could turn out the same as them.
explanation.definitionFit: To become similar to, or absorbed into, a group or culture.

clue.text: Cement found in sack, by the sound of it

indicators.note: says the letters are what is heard when the word is spoken

parts.note: sack means plunder, so loot

explanation.surface: Mortar was discovered inside a bag, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A clay or cement-like paste used to seal joints, as in chemistry apparatus.

clue.text: Girl can, wearing long hair, appear impregnable

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: the hair word is worn by the can, which has it around it

parts.note: a mane is long hair, as on a horse
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A girl with flowing locks, holding a tin, looks unbeatable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbreakable, as hard as diamond, so unconquerable.
